name: Athabaskan-Eyak
defining_innovation: The common ancestor of Eyak and the Athabaskan languages, whose close relationship Michael Krauss demonstrated in the 1960s.

chapters.title: Eyak's Relatives
chapters.body: Until the 1930s Eyak was hardly known. The anthropologist Frederica de Laguna recorded it, and in the 1960s **Michael Krauss** showed that it is the sister of the whole Athabaskan branch. It shares with Athabaskan the verb structure and the regular correspondences that allow Proto-Athabaskan-Eyak to be reconstructed, but it stands apart from all the Athabaskan languages in its vocabulary and sounds.

turning_points.title: Eyak and Athabaskan part
turning_points.description: The ancestors of Eyak settle on the south Alaskan coast, while those of the Athabaskans remain in the interior. The date is a rough estimate.

sources.citation: Krauss, Michael E. 1964. Proto-Athapaskan-Eyak and the problem of Na-Dene: The phonology. International Journal of American Linguistics 30(2): 118–131.
